aquae-sulis.file: Roman Baths and Abbey, IV, Bath, England-LCCN2002696370.jpg
aquae-sulis.caption: The Great Bath at Bath with the Abbey behind, a photochrom print of about 1890–1900. The pool is Roman, but the terraces, columns and statues around it are Victorian additions of the 1890s: a much later view.
aquae-sulis.author: Unknown photographer; photochrom print in the Library of Congress Photochrom Prints collection

augustine-canterbury-597.file: Luke St Augustine's Gospels Corpus Christi Cambridge MS 286.jpeg
augustine-canterbury-597.caption: St Luke, from the St Augustine Gospels (Cambridge, Corpus Christi College, MS 286), a 6th-century Italian gospel book long kept at Canterbury and traditionally, but not certainly, linked with Augustine's mission.
augustine-canterbury-597.author: Unknown Italian artist

battle-of-brunanburh-937.file: Alfred Pearseː The great battle of Brunanburh in 937 (Hutchinsons Story of the British Nation, 1922).jpg
battle-of-brunanburh-937.caption: 'The great battle of Brunanburh in 937', by Alfred Pearse, from Hutchinson's Story of the British Nation (1922): a much later imagining
battle-of-brunanburh-937.author: Alfred Pearse (1855–1933)

battle-of-hastings-1066.caption: Bayeux Tapestry, scene 57: King Harold is killed (embroidery made within a few years of the battle, probably in England in the 1070s)
battle-of-hastings-1066.author: Unknown embroiderers

battle-of-stamford-bridge-1066.caption: The Battle of Stamford Bridge, by Peter Nicolai Arbo (1870): a much later imagining
battle-of-stamford-bridge-1066.author: Peter Nicolai Arbo (1831–1892)

bede-historia-731.caption: A page (folio 3v) of the St Petersburg Bede, one of the earliest surviving copies of Bede's Ecclesiastical History, made in Northumbria within a few years of 731.
bede-historia-731.author: Unknown Northumbrian scribe

boudica-final-battle-60.file: Boadicea Haranguing the Britons (called Boudicca, or Boadicea) by John Opie.jpg
boudica-final-battle-60.caption: Boadicea haranguing the Britons: engraving by William Sharp after John Opie's history painting (published 1793). It is a much later imagining, not a record of the event or of how Boudica looked.
boudica-final-battle-60.author: William Sharp, after John Opie

camulodunum-destruction-60.file: Pictures of English History Plate IV - Boadicea and Her Army.jpg
camulodunum-destruction-60.caption: Boadicea and her army: colour print by Joseph Martin Kronheim from Pictures of English History (1868). It is a Victorian imagining of the revolt, not a depiction of Camulodunum or of any recorded scene.
camulodunum-destruction-60.author: Joseph Martin Kronheim

lindisfarne-gospels.caption: Opening page of St Matthew's Gospel (folio 27r), Lindisfarne Gospels, early 8th century; British Library, Cotton MS Nero D IV.
lindisfarne-gospels.author: Unknown Northumbrian scribe-artist (traditionally Eadfrith)

lindisfarne-raid-793.caption: Opening page of the Peterborough Chronicle (Anglo-Saxon Chronicle MS E, Bodleian Library MS Laud Misc. 636, written c. 1121), one of the manuscripts that records the raid under 793; this page is not the 793 entry
lindisfarne-raid-793.author: Scribes of Peterborough Abbey

synod-of-whitby-664.file: Benjamin Brecknell Turner - Whitby Abbey, Yorkshire, North Transept - Google Art Project.jpg
synod-of-whitby-664.caption: The north transept of Whitby Abbey, photographed by Benjamin Brecknell Turner in the 1850s. The ruins are of the 13th-century abbey, built long after the synod on the headland where the earlier monastery stood.
synod-of-whitby-664.author: Benjamin Brecknell Turner (1815–1894)

tintagel-trading-site.file: Tintagel, King Arthur's Castle from valley, II, Cornwall, England-LCCN2002696619.jpg
tintagel-trading-site.caption: Tintagel headland from the valley, a photochrom print of about 1890–1900. The ruins are of the 13th-century castle, much later than the post-Roman settlement; the title 'King Arthur's Castle' reflects the later legend, not the evidence.
tintagel-trading-site.author: Unknown photographer; photochrom print in the Library of Congress Photochrom Prints collection

william-lands-pevensey-1066.caption: Bayeux Tapestry, scene 38: Duke William's fleet crosses the sea and comes to Pevensey (embroidery of the 1070s)
william-lands-pevensey-1066.author: Unknown embroiderers
